transcript.content: Hi, welcome in — I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Um, I came in because... well, I just can't make myself go near the front windows at work anymore. Or really even that part of the street. I work in a store, and I keep finding excuses to just stay in the back room, even though being out on the floor is my actual job. It's just getting to be a problem.
When you think about standing near those front windows or being out on the street, what exactly goes through your mind about what might happen?

I don't know that I'm really thinking about something specific happening, honestly. It's more just... I get this awful, panicky feeling. Like my chest gets tight and I just know I need to get away from there. I guess I'm not really picturing a specific danger, it's just this overwhelming feeling that I'm not safe if I'm near the glass.
Before this fear started, did something frightening or traumatic happen to you near windows or on the street — like an assault, accident, or other scary event?

Yeah, um... about two weeks ago, actually. I was working an overnight shift at the store, and a car crashed right through the front window. So... well, that's when all this started. It's been going on ever since that happened.
Since the accident, have you been having unwanted memories, flashbacks, or nightmares about the crash itself?

Yeah, I have. It just keeps popping into my head out of nowhere, really. Like, I'll just be trying to set up displays, and... suddenly I can hear the bang again. I can just see the glass coming down like it's happening all over again right in front of me.
Since the crash, have you noticed feeling emotionally numb, detached from yourself or your surroundings, or like things around you seem unreal or dreamlike?

Yeah, actually, I have noticed something like that. Sometimes when I'm out on the sales floor, everything just feels... weird. Like the lights and the clothing racks seem really far away and kind of fake. It's hard to explain, but it almost feels like I'm watching myself move through the store instead of actually being there. It's just a really strange, detached feeling.
Have these symptoms—the flashbacks, avoidance, and feeling detached—been present continuously every day since the crash two weeks ago, or have they come and gone?

Um, I'm not really sure if it's been every single day. I haven't exactly kept track of it like that. It feels like it happens a lot, but... I don't know if it's constantly there or if it kind of comes and goes. I just know I've been dealing with it since the crash happened.
Since the crash, have you noticed yourself being unusually jumpy or easily startled, feeling constantly on edge, or having trouble sleeping?

Yeah, I've been really jumpy lately. It's like I'm constantly on edge. If a delivery cart bangs in the back room, or a car honks outside the store... or even if someone just walks up behind me when I'm not expecting it, I jump so hard. My whole body just jerks, and then my heart just keeps racing for a while afterward. It's really exhausting.
